subject: Request: subprocessor delegation matrix & country exemption clarification
messages:

Cc: legalops@finstream.com
Date: 2026-07-11T08:45:00Z
Subject: Request: subprocessor delegation & country exemption clarity

Hi Tessa,

We're preparing FinStream's DPA addendum review and need a concise subprocessor delegation matrix for the Redwood services we use. Specifically: 1) a CSV/matrix listing each subprocessor, country of processing, and whether they are used for prod vs staging; 2) any processors you consider "exempt" from cross-border transfer rules (e.g., ephemeral edge caches that only hold transient encrypted shards) and the justification; and 3) evidence of onshore fallbacks for APAC edge providers (we're particularly worried about SkyCache in Singapore).

Can you include a short statement about whether any subprocessor processes unencrypted PII outside the EU/APAC regions? Our privacy team also asked for an exported flow diagram showing egress paths for user_data -> telemetry/logging -> cache.

Timeline: we have a compliance review meeting next Wednesday (2026-07-15). Is it possible to get the matrix + evidence by EOD Monday (2026-07-13)?

Thanks,
Elise
Elise Carter
Privacy & Compliance Lead
FinStream

- Do you want the matrix limited to production-only subprocessors, or both prod + staging? (we can flag environment column)
- When you say "unencrypted PII," is your team using the same definition as in the DPA (user_identifiers + raw content)?

Plan: I'll coordinate with Kim to pull the up-to-date subprocessor matrix and with Markus for suggested DPA language around exemptions. We'll include a simple egress flow diagram and call out any processors that perform transient caching vs persistent storage.

We expect to deliver a packaged zip (matrix + flow-diagram + evidence checklist) by EOD Monday provided the scope is prod+staging. If you need prod-only, we can accelerate to EOD Sunday.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-11T14:20:00Z
Subject: Fwd: subprocessor matrix prep (draft attached)

Tessa / Markus — draft matrix attached. Notes:

- Attachments included: subprocessor_matrix_2026.xlsx, flow-diagram-edge.pdf
- SkyCache (SG) is classified as a transient edge-cache provider. We route through SkyCache for short-lived fragments only; things stored there are encrypted at rest and TTL < 5 minutes. We have an onshore fallback for APAC (EdgeOnshore) that can be enforced via routing policy if requested.
- LogiKeep (IE) handles log aggregation and retains logs up to 90 days; logs are pseudonymized by default for telemetry pipelines but full-text access is available to ops under tight controls — we flag this as a persistent processor in the matrix.
- Our working definition of "exempt" in the matrix is processors that only process encrypted fragments with no ability to reconstitute PII without Redwood-owned keys. Those are listed in the "exempt_rationale" column.
- Evidence we can provide: SOC2 snapshot for LogiKeep, encryption attestations for SkyCache, network routing policy (sample). I can assemble these into a single zip.

Open question for Legal: do we need customer-specific DocuSign approval for transient cache exceptions, or does the DPA's existing subprocessor clause (with notice) suffice?

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_matrix_2026.xlsx, flow-diagram-edge.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-12T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: subprocessor matrix prep (draft attached)

Thanks Kim — that matrix looks good as a draft. A couple of legal notes and suggested addendum language (attached dpa-addendum-draft.docx):

- For transient caching exceptions we typically ask for an explicit customer acknowledgement if the cache provider performs any processing within a jurisdiction that the customer has expressly restricted. If the provider only holds encrypted fragments and Redwood controls the keys, we can treat that as an operational exception without requiring DocuSign for each customer, provided we document the controls and include an opt-out in the addendum.
- Proposed short clause to include in the DPA addendum: "Redwood may engage transient caching processors for ephemeral, encrypted fragment storage; such processors shall not have access to plaintext personal data and will be used under documented routing policies. Customer may require onshore fallback routing for specified regions by providing written notice to Redwood.

I'll attach a redline to the DPA addendum for their legal team's review and include a DocuSign envelope link if they prefer a signed addendum.

Markus Klein
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
